This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed team is determined as the champion of the NBA for the 2026-27 season. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed team to be named as the champion of NBA for the 2026-27 season per the rules of NBA (e.g., participant is eliminated), the corresponding market will resolve to "No".

If multiple teams are declared winners, this market will resolve in favor of the team whose listed name comes first alphabetically.

If this event is cancelled, postponed after June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or a champion has not been declared within this timeframe, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source will be official information from the NBA: however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Young cores and recent roster continuity have elevated the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs to the top of trader consensus for the 2027 title, each carrying roughly 21 percent implied probability. Both franchises enter the 2026-27 season with established young talent, strong front-office drafting, and limited immediate cap constraints that support sustained contention. The Philadelphia 76ers and New York Knicks sit close behind on the strength of veteran anchors and recent playoff experience, while the rest of the field remains tightly bunched below 5 percent. This narrow distribution underscores how injury resilience, continued player development, and schedule difficulty can quickly shift long-term probabilities across a deep Western and Eastern Conference landscape.
